Use Case: Reveal Emerging Condition Trends to Grow Revenue
Description: Reveal Shifting Diagnosis Trends with Dataset Refresh Prioritization
Statement: The mix of conditions in the data captured by diagnosis_code over date_service shifts over time, and without tracking these trends the commercial team misses rising conditions that represent timely cohort-licensing opportunities for life-sciences clients.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code tracks diagnosis-code frequency over time, decomposes trend from seasonality to surface rising and declining conditions, and prioritizes which condition datasets to refresh and promote.
Business Value: The Commercial Data Product Manager prioritizes refreshing and promoting rising-condition cohorts, increasing timely licensable offerings measured by growth in diagnosis_code frequency over date_service [ESTIMATE: depends on diagnosis_code].
Priority Reasons: Surfacing rising conditions directs cohort-licensing promotion to timely opportunities, a recurring commercial decision closely tied to revenue expansion.
Quality Reasons: Signal from diagnosis_code frequency over date_service with distinct hvid and claim_type context: aggregate counts per diagnosis per month, apply STL decomposition and slope estimation to separate trend from seasonality, producing a condition_growth_slope KPI per diagnosis. ai_query interprets rising conditions and recommends refresh/promotion priorities, enabling timely licensable offerings [ESTIMATE: depends on diagnosis_code].

Use Case: Segment Patient Utilization to Grow Revenue
Description: Segment Patients by Clinical Utilization with Cohort Build Prioritization
Statement: HealthVerity licenses cohort datasets, but without data-driven patient utilization segments derived from hvid, diagnosis_code, and procedure_code, the commercial team cannot identify which patient groups are most valuable to package for life-sciences clients.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code engineers per-patient utilization features and applies K-Means clustering to discover natural patient segments, producing labeled cohorts the commercial team can prioritize for licensing offers.
Business Value: The Commercial Data Product Manager prioritizes which patient cohorts to package and license, increasing addressable cohort offerings measured by distinct hvid counts per segment and procedure diversity from procedure_code [ESTIMATE: depends on hvid].
Priority Reasons: Utilization segments identify which cohorts to package and license, a recurring commercial decision directly supporting revenue expansion.
Quality Reasons: Signal from per-hvid features: distinct diagnosis_code and procedure_code counts, claim_type mix, summed numeric-cast line_allowed and claim frequency. Standardized features feed K-Means to form utilization segments, producing a segment_value_profile. ai_query labels clusters and recommends which cohorts to prioritize for licensing, delivering addressable cohort offerings [ESTIMATE: depends on hvid].

Use Case: Anticipate Specialty Demand to Grow Revenue
Description: Forecast Specialty Demand Mix with Dataset Roadmap Recommendations
Statement: Changing procedure volume by provider taxonomy over date_service signals which clinical specialties are rising in activity, informing which specialty datasets to build ahead of client demand.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code builds monthly procedure volume series per taxonomy, forecasts near-term demand with Prophet, then calls ai_query to explain the trajectory and recommend a dataset build roadmap.
Business Value: The Product Roadmap Owner sequences specialty dataset builds against forecast demand, increasing count of datasets launched ahead of demand and reducing late-to-market specialty products [ESTIMATE: depends on procedure_code].
Priority Reasons: Forecasting specialty demand sequences dataset builds ahead of client demand, a recurring product decision directly tied to revenue capture.
Quality Reasons: Signal from date_service, procedure_code, prov_rendering_std_taxonomy and claim_id: aggregate monthly claim counts per specialty, fit Prophet forecasts with trend and seasonality to produce a projected_specialty_growth metric per taxonomy, rank by growth. ai_query explains trajectories and recommends a dataset build roadmap, delivering demand-aligned product sequencing [ESTIMATE: depends on procedure_code].

Use Case: Reveal Clinical Pathway Patterns to Grow Revenue
Description: Reveal Diagnosis-Procedure Co-Occurrence with Cohort Packaging Recommendations
Statement: The relationships between diagnoses and procedures captured in diagnosis_code and procedure_code across patient claims hold clinical-pathway value, but without mapping these co-occurrence networks the commercial team cannot design high-value condition-based cohort products.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code builds a co-occurrence graph linking diagnosis_code and procedure_code across claims, applies community detection to surface clinical pathway clusters, and recommends condition-based cohort products.
Business Value: The Commercial Data Product Manager designs condition-based cohort offerings from detected pathway communities, increasing packageable cohort products measured by linked diagnosis_code and procedure_code pairs per community [ESTIMATE: depends on diagnosis_code].
Priority Reasons: Clinical-pathway communities inform condition-based cohort product design, a recurring packaging decision tied to new licensable offerings and revenue.
Quality Reasons: Signal from within-hvid co-occurrence of diagnosis_code and procedure_code ordered by date_service: build a weighted GraphFrames graph, run community detection and centrality to find dense clinical pathway clusters, producing a pathway_community membership and strength metric. ai_query interprets each community and recommends condition-based cohort packaging, delivering packageable products [ESTIMATE: depends on diagnosis_code].

Use Case: Quantify Cohort Longevity to Grow Revenue
Description: Estimate Patient Observation Window Length with Panel Longevity Pricing Inputs
Statement: The length of time each hvid remains observable in the claims stream between first and last date_service determines how long a patient can be followed, a key driver of the price of longitudinal cohorts.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code derives per-patient first and last service dates, fits a Kaplan-Meier model treating last-observed as the event to estimate observation-window survival curves, then calls ai_query to explain retention segments and draft panel longevity pricing inputs.
Business Value: The Pricing Analyst uses observation-window survival estimates to set longitudinal cohort pricing tiers, increasing count of correctly-priced panels and reducing underpriced long-horizon cohorts [ESTIMATE: depends on date_service].
Priority Reasons: Observation-window survival estimates set longitudinal cohort pricing tiers, directly moving a pricing/revenue line through a recurring decision.
Quality Reasons: Signal from per-hvid min/max date_service derives observation window; treating last-observed as the event, a Kaplan-Meier model segmented by patient_state and diagnosis_code group estimates observation_window_survival curves. ai_query explains retention segments and drafts panel longevity pricing inputs, enabling correct longitudinal cohort pricing tiers [ESTIMATE: depends on date_service].

Use Case: Identify Care Setting Trends to Reduce Cost
Description: Reveal Service Site Shift Patterns with Site-of-Care Steering Recommendations
Statement: Shifts over time in where procedures are performed (place_of_service_std_id) for a given procedure_code reveal migration between higher and lower acuity settings that payer and life-science clients pay to understand.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code builds monthly procedure-by-site time series from date_service, applies STL decomposition to isolate directional site-of-care shifts, then uses ai_query to narrate the shift and recommend which site-of-care insight packages to prioritize.
Business Value: The Analytics Product Manager prioritizes which site-of-care insight packages to build, increasing count of billable analytic deliverables and reducing time spent on low-movement procedures [ESTIMATE: depends on place_of_service_std_id].
Priority Reasons: Site-of-care shift insight packages are directly billable analytic deliverables, tying the recurring prioritization decision to revenue.
Quality Reasons: Signal from date_service, procedure_code and place_of_service_std_id: build monthly claim_id count time series per procedure-by-site, apply STL decomposition and slope estimation to rank procedures by site_shift_magnitude. ai_query narrates each shift and recommends which insight packages to prioritize, delivering billable site-of-care deliverables [ESTIMATE: depends on place_of_service_std_id].

Use Case: Detect Billing Anomalies to Prevent Revenue Loss
Description: Detect Abnormal Provider Billing Patterns with Investigation Queue
Statement: Unusual billing behavior by rendering providers, visible across prov_rendering_npi, line_charge, and procedure_units_billed, can indicate upcoding or billing errors that distort real-world evidence quality and erode data trust with licensing clients.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code engineers per-provider billing features and trains an Isolation Forest to flag providers whose charge and unit patterns deviate from peers, producing a ranked investigation queue.
Business Value: The Data Quality Lead receives a ranked provider investigation queue, increasing the share of flagged anomalies in line_charge and procedure_units_billed reviewed before data release and preventing distorted claims from reaching clients [ESTIMATE: depends on line_charge].
Priority Reasons: Flagging abnormal billing protects RWD quality and data trust, mitigating a risk KPI; money effect is indirect via client trust and retention.
Quality Reasons: Signal from numeric-cast line_charge and procedure_units_billed, plus procedure_code and claim_type aggregated per prov_rendering_npi into mean charge, charge-per-unit and procedure diversity features. An Isolation Forest (contamination=0.05) scores providers, producing a billing_anomaly_score ranked queue. ai_query explains each flag, delivering a pre-release investigation queue [ESTIMATE: depends on line_charge].

Use Case: Classify Coding Completeness to Improve Data Quality
Description: Classify Claim Coding Completeness with Pre-Release Correction Actions
Statement: Incomplete or inconsistent coding across diagnosis_code, procedure_code, diagnosis_code_qual, and procedure_code_qual reduces the usability of claims for client analytics, yet claims are not scored for coding completeness before they are released.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code engineers coding-completeness features per claim and trains a classifier to tier claims by completeness, producing a pre-release correction worklist for the curation team.
Business Value: The Data Curation Lead works a pre-release correction list, increasing the share of fully-coded claims measured by populated diagnosis_code, procedure_code and their qualifier fields before client delivery [ESTIMATE: depends on claim_id].
Strategic Goals Alignment: Enable Data-Driven Decisions, Improve Customer Experience
Priority Reasons: Pre-release completeness scoring improves data usability for clients, a quality KPI with indirect revenue effect through product trust and retention.
Quality Reasons: Signal from diagnosis_code, procedure_code, diagnosis_code_qual, procedure_code_qual, revenue_code and claim_type per claim_id: engineer presence/validity and qualifier-consistency features, train a Random Forest to assign a completeness_tier per claim. ai_query explains low-tier claims and recommends corrections, producing a pre-release worklist that raises the share of fully-coded claims [ESTIMATE: depends on claim_id].

Use Case: Fill Specialty Coverage Gaps to Grow Revenue
Description: Predict Provider Taxonomy Specialty Gaps with Sourcing Prioritization List
Statement: Under-represented provider specialties in prov_rendering_std_taxonomy relative to the diagnosis and procedure mix they treat create coverage gaps that reduce the completeness of licensed specialty cohorts.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code clusters providers by their taxonomy and clinical activity profile using K-Means, identifies sparse specialty clusters against the diagnosis-procedure demand, then calls ai_query to explain gaps and draft a data sourcing prioritization list.
Business Value: The Data Acquisition Manager prioritizes which specialty data to source next, increasing count of complete specialty cohorts and reducing coverage gaps flagged by clients [ESTIMATE: depends on prov_rendering_std_taxonomy].
Priority Reasons: Identifying under-represented specialty cohorts guides which data to source next, enabling more complete sellable cohorts; revenue impact is one step removed via future licensing.
Quality Reasons: Signal from prov_rendering_std_taxonomy (specialty), distinct diagnosis_code and procedure_code counts and claim_id volume per prov_rendering_npi build per-provider feature vectors. K-Means clustering groups specialties and identifies sparse clusters against clinical demand, producing a specialty_coverage_gap metric. ai_query drafts a sourcing prioritization list, delivering completeness gains [ESTIMATE: depends on prov_rendering_std_taxonomy].

Use Case: Prevent Duplicate Billing to Protect Revenue
Description: Detect Duplicate Claim Submissions with Billing Integrity Review Queue
Statement: Identical or near-identical claims submitted under separate claim_id values for the same hvid, date_service, procedure_code and prov_billing_npi inflate reimbursement and distort data products sold to clients.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code engineers per-claim fingerprints from the billing fields, trains an Isolation Forest to flag statistically unusual duplicate clusters, then calls ai_query to explain each flagged cluster and draft a billing integrity review entry.
Business Value: The Data Quality Lead works a weekly review queue of suspected duplicate clusters, increasing the share of de-duplicated claims and reducing erroneous line_charge totals carried into licensed datasets [ESTIMATE: depends on line_charge].
Priority Reasons: De-duplication reduces erroneous charge totals carried into licensed datasets, a data-quality/risk KPI with indirect revenue effect.
Quality Reasons: Signal from grouping hvid+date_service+procedure_code+prov_billing_npi to form candidate duplicate clusters; features (claim_id count, line_charge variance, procedure_units_billed variance) feed an Isolation Forest that isolates abnormal duplicate clusters as a duplicate_risk_score. ai_query explains each cluster into a review-queue entry, reducing erroneous line_charge totals [ESTIMATE: depends on line_charge].

Use Case: Detect Reimbursement Gaps to Protect Revenue
Description: Detect Allowed-to-Charge Ratio Outliers with Pricing Review Queue
Statement: Variation between billed and allowed amounts in line_charge and line_allowed across procedures signals inconsistent reimbursement patterns that reduce the analytic reliability of the pricing dimension licensed to payer clients.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code models expected allowed amounts as a function of charge, procedure, and setting, flags claims whose actual allowed amounts deviate sharply from the model, and produces a pricing review queue.
Business Value: The Data Quality Lead reviews reimbursement-gap outliers before release, increasing the share of validated line_allowed values relative to line_charge and protecting the integrity of the licensed pricing dimension [ESTIMATE: depends on line_allowed].
Priority Reasons: Validating the pricing dimension protects the integrity of a licensed payer product, a quality/risk KPI with indirect revenue effect.
Quality Reasons: Signal from numeric-cast line_charge and line_allowed with procedure_code, place_of_service_std_id and claim_type as predictors: fit a Ridge/GLM predicting line_allowed, compute residuals and flag high-residual claims as a reimbursement_gap_outlier metric. ai_query explains outliers and drafts a pricing review queue, raising the share of validated allowed values [ESTIMATE: depends on line_allowed].

Use Case: Stabilize Payer Coverage to Grow Revenue
Description: Classify Payer Mix Instability with Dataset Positioning Actions
Statement: Variation in payer_type composition across regions and over date_service affects how representative a dataset is for commercial clients, and unstable payer mix lowers the sellable value of a cohort.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code engineers payer-mix features per region-period and trains a Random Forest to classify each segment as stable or volatile, then calls ai_query to explain drivers and recommend positioning actions for sales collateral.
Business Value: The Commercial Strategy Manager uses stability labels to decide which cohorts to promote, increasing count of well-positioned sellable datasets and reducing mispositioned pitches [ESTIMATE: depends on payer_type].
Priority Reasons: Stability labels guide which cohorts to promote and how to position them, supporting sellable dataset decisions tied to revenue.
Quality Reasons: Signal from payer_type share by patient_state over date_service with claim_id/hvid volume: engineer volatility features (share variance, entropy, trend slope) per region-period, train a Random Forest to label segments stable vs volatile as a payer_mix_stability class. ai_query explains drivers and drafts positioning actions, guiding which cohorts to promote [ESTIMATE: depends on payer_type].

Use Case: Close Demographic Gaps to Grow Revenue
Description: Classify Demographic Representativeness Gaps with Sampling Correction Actions
Statement: Imbalances in patient_gender, patient_year_of_birth and patient_state relative to clinical activity reduce how representative a cohort is, lowering its value for life-science clients requiring balanced panels.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code engineers demographic distribution features per condition cohort and trains a classifier to label cohorts as representative or skewed, then uses ai_query to explain the imbalance and recommend sampling correction actions.
Business Value: The Cohort Design Lead applies representativeness labels to decide which cohorts need sampling correction, increasing count of balanced sellable cohorts and reducing client-flagged demographic skew [ESTIMATE: depends on patient_year_of_birth].
Priority Reasons: Representativeness labels guide which cohorts need sampling correction, increasing balanced sellable cohorts and reducing client-flagged skew, tied to revenue one step removed.
Quality Reasons: Signal from patient_gender, patient_year_of_birth (derive age band) and patient_state relative to diagnosis_code cohorts per hvid: engineer skew features (deviation from expected distribution), train a Random Forest to label cohorts representative vs skewed as a representativeness_class. ai_query explains imbalances and drafts sampling correction actions, raising balanced sellable cohorts [ESTIMATE: depends on patient_year_of_birth].

Use Case: Flag Discharge Coding Errors to Ensure Compliance
Description: Detect Discharge Status Anomalies with Institutional Data Audit Queue
Statement: Inconsistent combinations of inst_discharge_status_std_id, inst_admit_type_std_id and inst_drg_std_id on institutional claims signal coding errors that undermine the clinical integrity of institutional data products.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code encodes institutional claim attribute combinations and trains an Isolation Forest to detect improbable discharge-admit-DRG combinations, then uses ai_query to explain each anomaly and generate an audit queue entry.
Business Value: The Clinical Data Auditor works an audit queue of improbable institutional coding combinations, increasing the share of validated institutional claims and reducing coding inconsistencies passed to clients [ESTIMATE: depends on inst_discharge_status_std_id].
Priority Reasons: Catching improbable institutional coding combinations improves clinical integrity of institutional products, a quality/risk KPI with indirect revenue effect.
Quality Reasons: Signal from inst_discharge_status_std_id, inst_admit_type_std_id, inst_drg_std_id and inst_type_of_bill_std_id on institutional claim_type claims: one-hot encode the combinations and train an Isolation Forest to flag improbable discharge-admit-DRG patterns as an institutional_anomaly_score. ai_query drafts audit-queue entries, raising the share of validated institutional claims [ESTIMATE: depends on inst_discharge_status_std_id].

Use Case: Prioritize Referral Hubs to Grow Revenue
Description: Reveal Referral Network Hubs with Provider Partnership Targeting
Statement: Referral relationships between prov_referring_npi and prov_rendering_npi form a provider network whose influential hubs indicate where data-partnership outreach yields the broadest patient coverage.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code constructs a referral graph from the referring and rendering NPI edges, computes PageRank and betweenness centrality with GraphFrames, then uses ai_query to profile top hubs and draft a partnership targeting list.
Business Value: The Partnerships Lead targets outreach to high-centrality provider hubs, increasing count of high-coverage partnerships and reducing wasted outreach to low-connectivity providers [ESTIMATE: depends on prov_referring_npi].
Priority Reasons: Referral-graph centrality identifies high-coverage partnership hubs, informing sourcing outreach that expands patient coverage; revenue link is one step removed through downstream licensing.
Quality Reasons: Signal from prov_referring_npi to prov_rendering_npi forms directed edges, weighted by distinct hvid count to measure patient coverage per referral. GraphFrames PageRank and betweenness centrality rank hub providers, producing a hub_centrality score per NPI. ai_query profiles top hubs into a targeting list, delivering coverage-maximizing partnership outreach [ESTIMATE: depends on prov_referring_npi].

Use Case: Classify Readmission Risk to Lower Risk
Description: Classify Institutional Readmission Risk with Care Signal Flags
Statement: Institutional claims carry discharge and admission signals in inst_discharge_status_std_id, inst_admit_type_std_id, and inst_drg_std_id, but these are not synthesized into a readmission-risk indicator that would make the dataset more valuable for payer and provider analytics clients.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code engineers per-patient institutional features and trains a Random Forest classifier to label patients by readmission-risk tier, producing a flagged cohort enriching the licensed dataset.
Business Value: The Clinical Data Scientist delivers readmission-risk tier labels per patient, increasing enriched-cohort coverage measured by institutional claim counts from claim_type and discharge statuses from inst_discharge_status_std_id available to analytics clients [ESTIMATE: depends on claim_id].
Priority Reasons: Readmission-risk tier labels enrich the licensed dataset for payer/provider clients, supporting a sellable enrichment tied to revenue one step removed.
Quality Reasons: Signal from institutional claims (claim_type=I) with inst_discharge_status_std_id, inst_admit_type_std_id, inst_drg_std_id, diagnosis_code and date_service: derive repeat institutional visits within a window as a label proxy, engineer discharge/admit/DRG/diagnosis-diversity features, train a Random Forest to assign a readmission_risk_tier per hvid. ai_query explains flags, delivering an enriched cohort [ESTIMATE: depends on claim_id].

Use Case: Predict Record Continuity to Improve Data Quality
Description: Predict Patient Longitudinal Continuity with Data Gap Remediation Actions
Statement: Longitudinal patient journeys depend on continuous claim activity per hvid over date_service, but patients who stop appearing create gaps that weaken the dataset's value for life-sciences research, and these drop-offs are not predicted in advance.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code models time-to-last-observation per patient using survival analysis to estimate continuity risk, producing a list of patients likely to drop from the longitudinal record for data gap remediation.
Business Value: The Clinical Data Scientist targets at-risk longitudinal records for enrichment, increasing retained continuous patient journeys measured by active hvid spans over date_service and improving dataset research value [ESTIMATE: depends on hvid].
Priority Reasons: Predicting longitudinal drop-off helps preserve continuous patient journeys that drive research value and dataset price; revenue link one step removed.
Quality Reasons: Signal from hvid and date_service yields per-patient observation start, last claim date and inter-claim gaps; event is prolonged absence of new claim_id. Kaplan-Meier and Cox PH models with claim frequency and diagnosis_code diversity covariates estimate a continuity_risk hazard per patient. ai_query drafts remediation actions, targeting at-risk journeys to retain continuous spans [ESTIMATE: depends on hvid].

Use Case: Identify Regional Claim Concentration to Grow Revenue
Description: Identify Geographic Claim Concentration with Market Expansion Targeting
Statement: Claim activity is spread unevenly across regions captured in patient_state and patient_zip3, and without quantifying this concentration the commercial team cannot target which geographies have the richest data to pitch to regional life-sciences and payer clients.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code aggregates claim and patient density by state and zip3, maps concentration intensity, and ranks geographies by data richness to produce a market expansion target list.
Business Value: The Commercial Data Product Manager prioritizes regional data offerings, increasing licensable coverage measured by distinct hvid and claim_id counts per patient_state and patient_zip3 [ESTIMATE: depends on claim_id].
Priority Reasons: Ranking geographies by data richness directs regional sales targeting, a recurring commercial decision directly supporting revenue expansion.
Quality Reasons: Signal from patient_state and patient_zip3 grouping distinct hvid and claim_id counts plus procedure_code diversity: compute per-region density and concentration metrics to produce a regional_data_richness score. ai_query explains high-value geographies and recommends expansion targets, delivering regional offering prioritization [ESTIMATE: depends on claim_id].

Use Case: Prioritize Provider Networks to Grow Revenue
Description: Prioritize High-Value Provider Networks with Data Partnership Targeting
Statement: Claim volume and charges concentrate among a subset of billing providers captured in prov_billing_npi, claim_id, and line_charge, but without quantifying this concentration the partnership team cannot focus data-sourcing efforts on the providers contributing the richest claim data.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code ranks billing providers by claim volume and charge contribution, applies Pareto analysis to isolate the vital few driving most data value, and produces a partnership target list.
Business Value: The Data Partnerships Manager focuses sourcing outreach on top-contributing providers, increasing high-value claim coverage measured by claim_id volume and line_charge share per prov_billing_npi [ESTIMATE: depends on line_charge].
Priority Reasons: Targeting the vital-few providers that contribute richest claim data directly supports data-sourcing to expand licensable coverage, a recurring commercial decision tied to revenue expansion.
Quality Reasons: Signal from prov_billing_npi (provider grain), claim_id (volume) and numeric-cast line_charge (value): aggregate distinct claim_id counts and summed line_charge per provider, rank and compute cumulative contribution for an 80/20 Pareto split, enrich with prov_billing_std_taxonomy. Produces a provider_contribution_share KPI and a vital-few target list, delivering partnership targeting [ESTIMATE: depends on line_charge].

Use Case: Flag Modifier Misuse to Ensure Compliance
Description: Reveal Procedure Modifier Overuse with Coding Review Prioritization
Statement: A small set of providers may concentrate disproportionate use of procedure modifiers (procedure_modifier_1 through procedure_modifier_4), a pattern associated with coding irregularities that reduce the trustworthiness of claims data.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code computes modifier-usage rates per provider, applies Pareto concentration analysis to isolate the top contributors to modifier volume, then uses ai_query to explain outlier providers and draft a coding review prioritization list.
Business Value: The Compliance Analyst prioritizes coding reviews on providers concentrating modifier use, increasing count of reviewed high-modifier providers and reducing modifier-related data-quality complaints [ESTIMATE: depends on procedure_modifier_1].
Priority Reasons: Prioritizing coding reviews on modifier-overuse providers reduces data-quality complaints, a quality KPI with indirect money effect.
Quality Reasons: Signal from procedure_modifier_1 through procedure_modifier_4 presence per prov_billing_npi across claim_id volume: compute a per-provider modifier_presence_rate, apply Pareto to isolate the top contributors to modifier volume. ai_query explains outlier providers and drafts a coding review prioritization list, reducing modifier-related data-quality complaints [ESTIMATE: depends on procedure_modifier_1].

Use Case: Forecast Claim Volume to Reduce Operational Cost
Description: Forecast Monthly Claim Volume with Capacity Planning Recommendations
Statement: Claim submission volume fluctuates over time across the dataset captured in date_service and claim_id, making it hard for data operations teams to plan ingestion and curation capacity, risking backlog and delayed data delivery to licensing clients.
Solution: Databricks Genie Code aggregates distinct claim_id counts by month derived from date_service, fits a time-series forecast, and projects future claim volume so the operations team can pre-allocate processing capacity.
Business Value: The Data Operations Manager uses the monthly claim-volume projection to schedule ingestion capacity ahead of demand, reducing processing backlog measured by claim counts per period from claim_id and improving on-time data delivery [ESTIMATE: depends on claim_id].
Priority Reasons: Operational capacity planning improves on-time data delivery but its revenue link is indirect; on synthetic sample data the forecast is illustrative, not a direct revenue mover.
Quality Reasons: Signal from date_service (temporal) and claim_id (volume) supports a monthly time series: parse date_service to month, count distinct claim_id per period to produce a claims_per_month KPI, then fit Prophet/ai_forecast with seasonality to project future volume. The projection feeds ingestion capacity scheduling, delivering the capacity planning outcome [ESTIMATE: depends on claim_id].
